national.title: Stevens endorses Rogers amid rift with El-Sayed

national.body: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed Michigan GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday amid a rift with Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed that has come front and center in the final sprint to Election Day. "Our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away, and he's right," Stevens said in a video posted on social media Sunday. national.title: Supermarket freezers in Belgium, Sweden and Luxembourg hit by suspected cyber-attack
national.summary: Stores in Sweden say temperatures for its freezers were raised to 50 C (122F).
national.body:
Dozens of supermarkets in Belgium and Sweden have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting its refrigerators and freezers.

Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while several ICA and Coop shops in Sweden were hit. Thirteen SuperValu shops have also been impacted in Ireland.

Millions of euros worth of food has had to be thrown away, according to local media reports, with one ICA store in Sweden saying temperatures for its freezers had been set to 50 C (122F).

It is not clear who is behind the attack, which follows a similar incident last month that affected hundreds of French supermarkets.

Both Belgium and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the incident.

Delhaize, one of Belgium's biggest supermarket chains, told Belgian media a "computer incident" had occurred overnight at 40 shops.

A Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart, in the Flemish Braband province in Flanders, told Het Laatste Nieuws it had lost €100,000 worth of produce.

The manager said that estimate did not even take into account further losses that would result from closing the shop.

national.summary: A historian says that colonial-era documents suggest the "King of the Pirates" and his violent crew got an assist from Thomas Jones, the namesake of Jones Beach.
national.body: An amateur historian has stumbled upon a provocative clue to the enduring mystery of what became of a notorious pirate who raided a royal Indian treasure ship centuries ago, implicating a co-conspirator whose name is familiar to many New Yorkers. James Bailey, who five years ago made headlines after unearthing ancient coins believed to be linked to English pirate Capt. Henry Every, now says that colonial-era documents suggest the "King of the Pirates" and his violent crew got an assist from Thomas Jones, the namesake of Jones Beach, New York's most visited state park after Niagara Falls. "You have millions of visitors and generations of New Yorkers going to this beach," Bailey said. "Nobody knew that he was actually a major player in arguably the biggest heist in the history of piracy." Since his big find, Bailey has pored through documents to dig even deeper into the bloody 1695 raid of the Ganj-i-Sawai on the Red Sea and the mystery of what happened to Every. The pirate crew is said to have tortured, killed and raped those aboard the royal ship, sparking global outrage and what is considered the first worldwide manhunt. Some were caught and executed, but many others, including Every, were never heard from again and are believed to have scattered to Europe and the American colonies.Documents, including depositions from Every's associates, suggest Jones was recruited to serve as a "wheelman," helping the pirates evade authorities after they made off with tens of millions of dollars' worth of gold and silver, according to Bailey. national.title: Jet from Texas crashes near homes in Palm Beach, Florida, killing 9 on board
national.summary: Details about what may have caused the crash had not yet been shared.
national.body: A business jet with nine people aboard nose-dived and crashed near homes in Palm Beach County, Florida, Sunday afternoon, killing everyone on board, officials said.No one on the ground was injured, Gov. Ron DeSantis told reporters at a news conference. Approximately 600 people were evacuated from the crash site near a mobile home park in Cresthaven, local officials said.The Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County just before 1 p.m., according to the Federal Aviation Administration. The agency said the aircraft had left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was bound for the Bahamas. Details about what may have caused the crash had not yet been shared."It was like a missile coming down and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere. And to have those people on board, it's really a tragic way to see people pass away," DeSantis said.Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed on X that all nine people on board have died."Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost," Duffy wrote.Air traffic control audio captured the pilot's last communications with the ATC tower before the aircraft went down. The pilot can be heard saying they were descending 10,000 feet per minute, according to the audio on LiveATC.net. The pilot later declared an emergency, yelling, "We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute."The pilot is later heard telling the tower: "We're gonna crash ... national.title: Two economists studied California's billionaire tax. They reached wildly different conclusions
national.summary: What happens in California could shape how America taxes the superrich. But will its billionaire tax fill state coffers — or drain them?
national.body:
In 1978, California voters approved Proposition 13, a historic tax revolt that became an opening salvo in the Reagan revolution and its national movement to slash taxes. Now, Californians are voting on Proposition 40, which could prove to be just as revolutionary — but in the opposite direction: it would create America's first-ever wealth tax targeted at billionaires.

As Election Day approaches, economists have been duking it out over this proposed wealth tax. It could provide a sort of nerdy preview of a coming national fight over taxing the superrich. Will this wealth tax help rein in runaway inequality and fill the state's coffers — or will it convince billionaires to fire up their private jets and set up residence in mansions outside the state? Some megabillionaires have already fled California since the tax was proposed.

"If California says, 'We can tax billionaires. We can tax the wealthiest, most powerful people in the world,' it will be the beginning of not only a broader U.S.-wide movement, ultimately paving the way for a federal wealth tax — but I think it will be the beginning of an international movement," Zucman tells Planet Money .

On the other side of the debate is Stanford economist and Hoover Institution senior fellow Joshua Rauh. His analysis, co-authored with Benjamin Jaros, comes to a wildly different conclusion: the tax could lead to an exodus of billionaires out of California, damaging the state's economy and blowing a hole in the income tax revenue the state already collects from billionaires.

" It would not raise $100 billion for the state," Rauh argues. Instead, he estimates, this tax could actually end up draining California's state coffers. " We calculate that Proposition 40 would cost the state of California $39 billion."

It's a classic Berkeley-Stanford rivalry, but the stakes are much higher than a football game. California voters are deciding whether to pursue a historic wealth tax experiment, which could influence tax policy around the nation, even the world. Indeed, the superrich, fearing that this wealth tax could spark a widespread movement, have poured a staggering $333 million into a group trying to defeat this proposition, according to a recent report in The New York Times .

The wealth tax Prop 40 proposes is pretty straightforward: a one-time, 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires, with some assets exempted. It would apply retroactively to any billionaire who was a resident of California on January 1, 2026. The money would be earmarked mostly for the health care of low-income Californians, to help offset federal cuts to Medicaid.

national.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
national.summary: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.
national.body:
Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff and confirmed airfares will be "materially higher" next summer because of a sharp rise in fuel costs following the US-Israel war with Iran.

The airline said it expects fuel prices to remain high "well into 2027" unless there is a "swift resolution" to the conflict.

Ryanair said its fuel bill is forecast to be €2bn (£1.6bn) higher in the short-term and its chief executive, Michael O'Leary, said airfares would have to rise by "double-digits" to help cover the cost.

But the firm said that was unlikely to be enough and it is looking into "temporary pay freezes". Unite, the union which represents Ryanair staff, has been contacted for comment.

The airline said its pre-tax profits fell by 16% to €2.4bn during the six months to the end of September, largely due to higher fuel costs jumping by 15%.

Ryanair said its fuel bill is forecast to be €2bn higher in the short-term.

The company said that although 80% of its fuel bill had been "hedged" – in effect, bought in advance at fixed prices – the cost of the remainder was elevated.

O'Leary reiterated forecasts from earlier this year Ryanair would "need a 20% fare increase" to cover the cost of jet fuel.

national.summary: Maria Montserrat Alvarado, a 39-year-old U.S. media executive, becomes the new head of Vatican communications this week, the first laywoman to head a Vatican "ministry."
national.body: Maria Montserrat Alvarado, a 39-year-old U.S. media executive, becomes the new head of Vatican communications this week, the first laywoman to head a Vatican "ministry." The Mexican American will also be the first non-Italian to lead a vast department overseeing all of the Vatican's television, radio and print operations, as well as its press office. Analysts say the appointment of a professional woman to the key post signals that Pope Leo views women differently from his predecessors at the Vatican, where nuns have tended to be the women holding senior positions. Her appointment, announced in June, came as a surprise even to Alvarado. "I didn't apply, I wasn't chosen" through a standard application process, she said in a television interview with U.S. Catholic media outlet EWTN News, where she has served as president and chief operating officer since 2023. It was "an appointment from the Holy Father," U.S.-born Pope Leo XIV said of the new role for Alvarado, who uses the name "Montse."EWTN News is the news division of the Eternal Word Television Network, the largest Catholic television network in the United States, which was founded by a nun and has established itself as a touchstone for conservative Catholics. It hasn't always had a warm relationship with the Vatican. Certain programs on the network developed a reputation for their criticism of Leo's Argentine predecessor, Pope Francis, a reform-minded pontiff who angered some within the Church's conservative wing, particularly in the U.S. In 2021, Francis appeared to call them out on it, bemoaning a "major Catholic television channel that is constantly criticizing the pope." "I may personally deserve attacks and insults because I am a sinner, but the Church does not deserve this; it is the work of the devil," he said. Alvarado was a presenter for EWTN at that time.Alvarado's backgroundBorn in Mexico, Alvarado arrived in the U.S. as a child and grew up in Miami before moving to Washington to pursue her studies. national.summary: Trump must decide whether to end the war or return to it, Iran says, as both sides trade threats, but keep diplomacy alive.
national.body: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson said Monday that the next move in the standoff with the United States is for President Trump to make. "The ball is in the U.S. court, because our demands have been stated very clearly and transparently, and Iran's demands are reasonable and logical," Esmaeil Baqaei told journalists in Tehran. Baqaei said ongoing negotiations, which have been brokered by Qatar, Pakistan and other mediators, were centered around the a seven-day proposal that Iran originally presented to the U.S. side in September, which calls for frozen Iranian assets to be released, the U.S. naval blockade to be lifted and an end to fighting on all fronts, in exchange for the phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and further negotiations on other topics. President Trump rejected the initial proposal, but both sides have since exchanged revisions, and Mr. Trump has said repeatedly in recent weeks that he just needs to make a decision on whether to launch new attacks on Iran, or to make a deal to end the war. Speaking Sunday to a radio network ahead of a campaign rally in Iowa, Mr. Trump said he would finish with the war soon, "one way or the other." "Either they'll make a deal, or we'll just end it," he said, without offering any further context.

national.title: 6 things to watch for on election night
national.summary: Some of the key storylines to watch will center around various voters groups that have soured on President Trump during his second turn out.
national.body:
It can be hard to know what to focus on in midterm elections. There are so many races, from elections for governor and senator to the House and state legislatures. For a better idea of how the night might go to see which party might control Congress, here are six things to watch:

There are two states, Indiana and Kentucky, that will see results in the 6 p.m. ET hour. And then there's Florida, which is split between the Eastern and Central time zones. But most of the state is on Eastern time. So lots of House race results will be coming in during the 7 p.m. ET hour, even if statewide contests like the Senate and governors races won't be called at the earliest until 8 p.m. ET.

Some races to watch for early indicators of what might come later in the evening — Indiana's 5th Congressional District, Kentucky's 6th and Florida's 22nd and 27th. Indiana's 5th and Kentucky's 6th are seats held by Republicans that are more competitive now than at the beginning of the cycle. If these are close or tipping to Democrats, it could be a sign of low Republican turnout and a bigger Democratic wave.

Florida's 22nd is held by a Democrat but redrawn to tip in Republicans' favor. Trump won Florida's 27th by double-digits so this heavily Latino district could be an indicator of how this key subgroup votes.

Independents are a key swing group, but they are also a lower-propensity voting group in midterms.

It used to be that Republicans had to win a bigger share of independents before the Trump era. Mitt Romney, for example, won 55% of independents in 2012 but lost the presidential election. But there's been a political realignment in this country with blue-collar white voters trending toward Trump, fewer people identifying as Democrats and better-educated white voters shifting toward Democrats.

So in the decade since Trump has been on the political scene, Republicans have done well when they win at least 46% of independents. When they haven't, they've lost.

The Michigan Senate race is important for control of the Senate. If Republicans flip it, the magic number for Democrats goes from four to five, meaning Democrats would have to win five seats held by Republicans to win control of the Senate.

national.title: When it comes to election pressure, this year's Georgia or Michigan could be anywhere
national.summary: The districts that will decide control of the House and Senate next year are spread across the country. Voting officials in those places may face scrutiny and pressure they've never experienced.
national.body:
There's one big difference, Tina Barton says, between running an election in a battleground state and a non-battleground.

"If a human error happens, it's easily explained in the press and it's not a story," Barton says. "You have a human error in a battleground state and all of a sudden it can become a massive conspiracy."

In 2020, she oversaw elections as city clerk of Rochester Hills, Mich. On election night, her office mistakenly sent an unofficial absentee vote file twice because the first one didn't initially appear to send.

Elections Justice Department issues subpoenas to California election workers Such mistakes happen every election cycle in a national process run by tens of thousands of human beings. A machine isn't plugged in. A poll worker sleeps through their alarm clock and doesn't open a precinct on time. Someone gets handed the wrong ballot.

In Barton's case, the issue didn't impact actual votes, and it was corrected in the tally the following day.

The chairwoman of the Republican National Committee accused her office of improperly giving votes to Democrats, and Barton received a rush of death threats, including a voicemail saying she deserved a "throat to the knife" because she had "frauded out America of a real election."

More than half a decade later, for better or worse, election officials in swing states like Michigan, Georgia and Arizona are more used to that level of pressure and scrutiny.

In this year's midterms, however, because the races that will decide control of the U.S. House and Senate are spread around the country, local officials in places like Iowa, Alaska, New York and Kansas may find themselves in the national spotlight for the first time.

She'd become distraught, telling her mom on the phone that she felt sad and lonely, that she desperately wanted a hug, that she was getting nosebleeds and thought she had an infection.Meanwhile, as her mother, Carmen, was going through the process to regain custody, federal immigration officials instead arrested her, sending her to a Louisiana detention center though she had a pending asylum case and no criminal record."Both of us are trapped," Carmen said in a September interview from the detention center. national.title: Robots strut their stuff, race up sacred China mountain
national.summary: Dozens of robots took on more than 3,000 steps up one of China's most famous peaks, many carrying eggs and watermelons in a race organizers billed as a test of real-world machine endurance, state media showed.
national.body: Dozens of robots took on more than 3,000 steps up one of China's most famous peaks Monday, many carrying eggs and watermelons in a race organizers billed as a test of real-world machine endurance, state media showed. For hundreds of years, Mount Tai -- the tallest peak in China's eastern Shandong province -- was an important pilgrimage for Chinese emperors, and it features prominently in Chinese mythology. But the rugged terrain would prove a stern test for some competitors. One humanoid robot wearing a bandana collapsed in a heap on the cobbled route before engineers rushed in to repair it, while another tumbled down a flight of stairs and came to rest beside a rubbish bin. The UNESCO World Heritage site hosted technologies of the future as part of a new World Mountain Robot Challenge, footage from state broadcaster CCTV showed. Over a 2.4-mile course with more than 1,970 feet of ascent, robots and their engineers from around 90 teams were tasked with either completing the route as fast as possible or transporting fragile goods such as fresh eggs and watermelons to the summit. A canine robot made by Beijing Lingyi Technology -- a subsidiary of industry giant Unitree -- completed the course in 43 minutes, 41 seconds, to win the four-legged speed category. Most tourists take at least two hours to complete the route, according to CCTV.The fastest humanoid robot -- belonging to Beijing-based team Zhishen Lingyue -- completed a shorter race course in 27 minutes and 26 seconds. Organizers called Mount Tai's rocky terrain a "natural extreme testing ground" that could help train robots for real-world use, local media reported. Veteran lifestyle guru Martha Stewart has admitted she "really screwed up" by dressing as a homeless person for Halloween.

The 85-year-old US entrepreneur and personality has deleted a photo of herself wearing torn clothes and dirt on her face, holding a sign saying: "I am hungry help me!!"

She posted a statement on Sunday saying she was "distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention".

That was followed by a fuller apology. "It's hard to admit when you've really screwed up. My earlier statement didn't go far enough. I know many people are suffering economically. Wearing a costume like I did was insensitive and not funny. I am very sorry."

Stewart had captioned her original Instagram photo: "My QVC candles are perfect for Halloween!!!"

"This sartorial take on a homeless person is a lot. Insulting? Demeaning? Confusing? All of the above," PR expert Molly McPherson wrote , external .

One person wrote on social media: "Why in the hell would you even think about wearing that as a costume?"

Another said: "Why would she do that? Who did she think would find that funny? Billionaires?"

national.title: Nine killed as small jet crashes on Florida street
national.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the crash, which happened near President Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort, as a "horrific tragedy".
national.body:
A business jet crashed in a neighbourhood in Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people on board, the US transport secretary has said.

The crash happened near Cresthaven, some nine miles (14 km) from Mar-a-Lago, President Donald Trump's resort in the wealthy enclave of Palm Beach County, around 12:50 EST (17:50 GMT).

Images show a large crater in the middle of a multi-lane road, with fire and debris from the Learjet 60 aircraft scattered across it, but nobody on the ground was hurt.

The aircraft had departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a statement.

Flight analysis indicates that the jet was plummeting hundreds of feet per second before crashing.

In air traffic control audio recorded moments before the crash, someone in the cockpit can be heard reporting "moderate turbulence" and that the crew was "managing the ice".

The person can then be heard saying the plane was "picking up precipitation" and "we need to climb". Moments later, the same voice said the plane was descending at a rate of 10,000ft (3,048m) per minute.

The crew member declared an emergency, yelling "we are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000ft per minute", before saying, "we are going to crash into the ground".

national.title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
national.summary: The country was the first to contribute troops to the AU mission established to stabilise Somalia in 2007.
national.body:
Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly two decades of military involvement in the country.

The first contingent of 109 Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) troops reportedly left the capital, Mogadishu, on Friday, following an announcement by Uganda's army chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba.

Uganda's acting army spokesperson, Chris Magezi, did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

Uganda was the first African country to deploy troops to Somalia under the African Union Mission in Somalia (Amisom), which was established in 2007 to help protect the country's transitional government from attacks by Islamist militants.

Last week, Gen Muhoozi said Uganda had begun pulling out its troops and would hand over security responsibilities to Somali forces.

"As we promised, we have started withdrawing UPDF from Somalia. After 20 years of a lot of blood and sacrifice, we are handing over security to our Somali brothers," he wrote on X.

The withdrawal is being carried out in phases and is expected to be completed in August 2027.

However, Uganda is not ending its entire military involvement in Somalia. Its troops deployed under a separate bilateral security arrangement will remain in the country.

national.title: Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences
national.summary: The author of Jasper Jones and Runt pleaded guilty in May after police raided his home months earlier.
national.body:
Australian children's author Craig Silvey has been sentenced to seven months in jail for possessing and distributing child exploitation material.

In handing down her sentence, Judge Hayley Cormann called Silvey's actions "repulsive" and "degrading".

In January, Silvey was arrested after police raided his home in Western Australia and seized several electronic devices. In May, the 44-year-old pleaded guilty to possessing and distributing child exploitation material and in October he was jailed pending his sentencing.

The father-of-three is best known for his award-winning young adult novel Jasper Jones and children's book Runt, both of which were later made into movies.

"You have devastated and betrayed the trust of thousands of people, and you've let entire communities down," Cormann said on Monday, according to WA Today.

Police said Silvey had online chats, in which he discussed child exploitation, open at the moment they turned up to raid his house.

In them, the court heard, Silvey had described himself as "extremely open minded" and "obsessed with taboos".

He'd discussed his sexual interest in children as young as five with another user of a pornography site, and detectives found images and videos of other adults abusing children on his devices.

national.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack
national.summary: The exchange froze transactions following the incident which has been linked to a North Korean group.
national.body:
Binance customers withdrew $3.6bn (£2.7bn) of assets from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following what is believed to be the largest hack in history.

The firm suspended all transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets.

Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber-attack .

The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach but the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack.

Binance said on X: "Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion."

There was an "initial spike" in withdrawals, which later declined and "are stabilising as expected", it added.

Sunday's net withdrawals account for just over 2% of the $171bn of assets under its management, said Binance.

The firm said last week that it has reserved more than $6.3bn in funds, to deal with ​the fallout of the attack.

The Minnesota Vikings became the last NFL team to lose their unbeaten record as the 2026 season continued with a wild weekend.

There were a number of rare occurrences during week eight while two games were settled in overtime.

The Dallas Cowboys and the Kansas City Chiefs were both beaten after being stunned by late fightbacks while quarterback Joe Burrow was involved in six touchdowns as the Cincinnati Bengals won again.

Otherwise running backs shone on Sunday, especially for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they managed to claim victory without completing a single pass.

And the Baltimore Ravens lost not one but two quarterbacks during their defeat by the Buffalo Bills, including the league's two-time Most Valuable Player, Lamar Jackson.

Two former MVPs went head-to-head as Lamar Jackson returned from three games out with an ankle injury to face Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills.

But that match-up was ruined within moments as Jackson injured his right thumb on the game's first snap, and his back-up Tyler Huntley was then ruled out in the second quarter with a toe injury.

That meant they had to finish the game with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback and Buffalo ran out comfortable 36-10 winners.

national.title: UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years
national.summary: The U.N.'s long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.
national.body:
FILE - A Sahrawi refugee boy stands in the shadow in the Boujdour refugee camp, Oct. 11, 2021. Bernat Armangue/AP hide caption

CASABLANCA, Morocco — The U.N.'s long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years, as a result of a U.S.-Russia standoff at U.N. headquarters over the territory's future.

The end of the mission raises concerns about stability in the region. Rich in minerals and fisheries, Western Sahara is a vast desert territory roughly the size of Colorado along Africa's northwestern Atlantic coast. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.

"This 1 November 2026 marks the start of the liquidation period," Stéphane Dujarric, spokesperson for the U.N. secretary general, said in a statement. "A smaller team reporting to the United Nations' Department of Operational Support will oversee the orderly transportation of assets belonging to troop-contributing countries to their respective nations, and the appropriate disposal of equipment belonging to the United Nations.''

The mission had been repeatedly extended since it was established in 1991. In the U.N. Security Council on Friday, Russia vetoed a draft U.S. resolution that would have supported Morocco's demand for sovereignty over Western Sahara and ended the peacekeeping mission next year.

World What really happened in Ceuta? Why we may never find out Then a rival Russian resolution to extend the mission was voted down. The disagreement led to an abrupt end of the force's mandate.

Morocco's royal palace welcomed the non-renewal of the mission. It called it an "instrument to internationalize the dispute.''

The Polisario Front, backed by Algeria, called it "an unacceptable decision.'' The Algerian foreign ministry said it profoundly regrets the non-renewal of the mandate and criticized what it called the ''excessive bias'' of the U.S. draft resolution.

national.title: 9 dead as jet nosedives and erupts into fireball near busy roadway in South Florida
national.summary: U.S. Transportation Secretary Duffy says all nine people died aboard a business jet that crashed into a Florida neighborhood. The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas.
national.body:
Law enforcement respond to a plane crash in Palm Beach County, Fla., on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Mark Elias/AP hide caption

A business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes near a busy roadway. Everyone on board was killed, the nation's transportation secretary said.

Video recorded by people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky before striking near the Palm Beach County roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining a crater as people milled about, expressing shock that it landed only feet from homes and inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy posted on X that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County at 12:50 p.m. and called it a "horrific tragedy." The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation, he said.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed.

"It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis told reporters at the scene. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road."

Rain pounded the region on Sunday. A flood watch due to excessive rainfall was in effect through Monday afternoon, the National Weather Service said.

The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.

national.title: Iran killed her teenage daughter - now she is facing up to the regime
national.summary: Samira's 16-year-old daughter Sevda was shot dead as they took part in mass protests in January.
national.body:
"I worked in sales in Iran. I sold cosmetics," she tells BBC Panorama.

But that all changed the day her only child was shot dead in front of her by Iranian security forces. Sixteen-year-old Sevda was taking part in protests against Iran's repressive regime that engulfed the country earlier this year - before the US and Israel launched widespread air strikes which killed the country's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Samira's grief became fury as Iran's authorities then hindered, rather than helped, her search for her daughter's body, she says.

"I realised that finding Sevda wasn't the end, but just the beginning of all the harassment they put me through."

Samira made a dramatic escape from Iran on foot, navigating dangerous mountainous terrain.

She now lives abroad in hiding, describing herself as a "one-woman army fighting the regime". In a search for accountability and justice after her daughter's death, she is intent on naming the members of the security forces and officials she believes were responsible for firing fatal shots during the protests.

"They'll bring me to the brink of death before they kill me, but finding me won't be easy… Return to normal life? There is no going back," she says.

Samira is among several Iranians the BBC has spoken to since the start of the year. Some, still inside the country, told Panorama they wanted to speak out despite the risks, saying they had found it difficult to hold on to hope once the mass protests had been brutally crushed.

President Trump told reporters that he'd spoken with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday and had a "very good talk with him."

Mr. Trump gave no details but said the two had discussed the war in Iran.

There was no public comment on the call from Netanyahu, who some Israelis have worried might be eager to attack Iran again to salvage his political standing after he and his allies lost their majority of seats in parliament after last week's elections.

The president was speaking to Right Side Broadcasting Network before a campaign rally in Iowa on Sunday.

national.title: Trump makes final campaign push in final weekend before election
national.summary: The US president rallied in states that Republicans previously won - showcasing how tight Tuesday's elections could be in determining control of Congress.
national.body:
In the last weekend before the pivotal midterm elections, US President Donald Trump has made a final pitch to voters in hopes of keeping Republicans in control of Congress.

Trump held rallies in Florida, Iowa and Kansas - states he won in past elections - in a sign of Republicans' defensive stance ahead of Tuesday's vote.

Facing voter frustration over rising prices, Trump sought to tamp down such concerns and shift focus on attacking Democrats, saying they would "bankrupt" families if elected.

Polls suggest that Democrats have a good chance at winning at least partial control of Congress, which would act as a check on Trump's power and could upend the last two years of his presidency.

Trump has been campaigning non-stop across the country ahead of the election - even in areas that were once thought to be safe Republican strongholds.

Throughout the weekend, Trump made the case for his party at rallies in Kansas, Florida and Iowa as well as at tele-rallies for candidates in states including Michigan, Ohio and Pennsylvania.

In previous years, Trump easily won Florida, Iowa and Kansas - once considered reliably Republican states - but the president's visits there in the final days of his election drive highlighted just how competitive these states have become in determining control of Congress.

national.summary: China Media Group, which acknowledged Mbappé's apology, has not said how long the blackout will last.
national.body:
China's state broadcaster CCTV did not air a Real Madrid match on Sunday, despite the club's star striker Kylian Mbappé's apology for his "ill-judged" remarks on the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Mbappé drew huge backlash after saying the meme "that makes [him] laugh the most" was the one in which his face is superimposed on a "Chinese dictator" resembling Mao.

China Media Group, CCTV's parent organisation, said last Tuesday it would suspend broadcasts of Spanish football La Liga matches following the furore, which also led to Mbappé being dropped by several Chinese brands.

China's foreign ministry had said it took Mbappé's apology "seriously". Real Madrid and La Liga have also apologised.

China Media Group had earlier demanded apologies from the three parties, calling them "an absolute prerequisite" for moving past the incident.

It has acknowledged the apologies, but has not commented on how long the broadcast blackout will last.

Mbappé, who reportedly made his remark about the meme on French talk show The Bridge, apologised later on Tuesday.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," he had said.

local.title: Rochester Board of Education outlines its priorities for state lawmakers
local.summary: The Rochester city school board is preparing its legislative priorities going into 2027.
local.body:
Listen • 0:56 The Rochester city school board is preparing its legislative priorities going into 2027.

The board develops those priorities each year ahead of the state's legislative session, which begins in January.

A potential moratorium on opening new charter schools is one of several proposed priorities that the board highlighted.

The board also wants lawmakers to boost state funding for community schools, Medicaid-supported mental health services, and career and technical training programs — with emphasis on programming for disabled students as they transition into young adulthood.

"We have BOCES and we have other programs," board member Kareem McCullough said during a meeting this week. "But looking for funding to go along with that special service aid would be beneficial in making sure that those particular students get to transition out of school into that adult life."

In a 2027 Legislative Priorities Feedback document, the board stated that "Urban districts like RCSD face unique funding and access challenges in providing these specialized opportunities," referring to career and technical education for students with disabilities.

The board also emphasized in that document that there needs to be adequate state funding for special education services.

About 5,000 of the district's 22,000 students are classified as having a disability, according to RCSD data.

local.title: That extra 'fall back' hour of sleep may not be as restful as you think
local.summary: AAA says even though we had an extra hour to sleep, falling back can make drivers tired because their internal clock is suddenly out of alignment with their daily schedule.
local.body:
Eastern Standard Time began on Sunday, when we set our clocks back one hour.

And even though the switch is often billed as "an extra hour of sleep," the time change can cause drowsiness as our internal clocks work to realign with our daily schedule.

That's why the New York state Department of Transportation and AAA are issuing reminders of the hazards of drowsy driving.

Sleepy drivers can actually lose consciousness for a few seconds, according to research from AAA's Foundation for Traffic Safety. They call these "micro sleeps."

"Having a really long blink, your eyes closing for even just a couple of seconds, you are driving your vehicle pretty much the distance of a football field with your eyes closed," said Valerie Puma, a spokesperson for AAA of Western and Central New York.

Fatigue was a factor in 3,371 police-reported crashes in New York state in 2025, according to preliminary data from the Institute for Traffic Safety and Management.

AAA's safety tips for drivers include: Eliminating cellphones and other distractions, leaving extra distance between your vehicle and the one in front of you, and to be watchful for pedestrians, cyclists, and wildlife, especially during the darker afternoon and evening hours.

"Don't underestimate the power of a power nap," Puma added. "I've done it several times on longer road trips, finding a safe place to just take an extra 15, 20 minutes to rest before you get back on the road."

Dr. Sidhu brings extensive training in pulmonary and critical care m
local.body:
Brooks-TLC Hospital System (BTLC) is pleased to welcome Mandeep Sidhu, MD, a physician specializing in pulmonology and critical care medicine, enhancing specialized respiratory (lung) care for patients throughout Chautauqua County.

Dr. Sidhu brings extensive training in pulmonary and critical care medicine, internal medicine and geriatric medicine. Her clinical focus includes diagnosing and treating complex lung conditions, managing acute and chronic respiratory illnesses and caring for critically ill patients who require advanced respiratory support.

Dr. Sidhu completed a fellowship in pulmonary disease and critical care at the University of Illinois Chicago and Jesse Brown VA Hospital. She also completed a fellowship in geriatric medicine at the University of Illinois Chicago and an internal medicine residency at Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center at the Permian Basin. She earned her Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree from Guru Gobind Singh Medical College, India.

Dr. Sidhu's hospital-based expertise includes the management of acute and chronic respiratory failure, pneumonia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma exacerbations, sepsis and other critical illnesses. Her experience includes managing patients who require invasive mechanical ventilation or noninvasive respiratory support, as well as evaluating complex pulmonary conditions in collaboration with hospitalists, emergency medicine physicians, nurses, respiratory therapists and other specialists.

In addition to inpatient care, Dr. Sidhu will help patients manage a range of pulmonary conditions through outpatient evaluation and follow-up. She is accepting new patients for pulmonary function tests (PFTs). PFTs are noninvasive tests that measure how well the lungs work, including how much air a person can breathe in and out and how efficiently the lungs transfer oxygen. PFTs help physicians diagnose and monitor conditions such as asthma, COPD, emphysema and other lung diseases.

Dr. Sidhu said her decision to pursue medicine was initially inspired by her father's dream of seeing her become a physician. Throughout her training, that inspiration grew into a commitment to helping patients and families navigate some of their most challenging health experiences.

"Over time, I discovered that medicine was not just about fulfilling a dream, but also about making a meaningful difference in people’s lives," Dr. Sidhu said. "I find it especially rewarding to combine medical knowledge, critical thinking and compassion to help patients through some of their most difficult times. Caring for patients and supporting their families is what makes being a physician so meaningful to me."

local.title: Jayhawks capture Region 3 crown, heading to NJCAAs
local.summary: BATAVIA — On a crisp, breezy Saturday afternoon, the Jamestown Community College women’s soccer team found an inner fire in the second half of its Region 3 championship matchup against fifth-ranked Mohawk Valley CC, claiming the crown and a spot in the national tournament with a thrilling 2-1 victor
local.body:
BATAVIA -- On a crisp, breezy Saturday afternoon, the Jamestown Community College women's soccer team found an inner fire in the second half of its Region 3 championship matchup against fifth-ranked Mohawk Valley CC, claiming the crown and a spot in the national tournament with a thrilling 2-1 victory.

"What these 16 players have accomplished is incredible," said Jayhawks' head coach Sarah Chimera. "They have worked hard, supported one another, put the team ahead of themselves and continued to find ways to get better all season. I'm just so proud of them. Winning a Region 3 championship is an amazing accomplishment, but seeing the team they've become and what they've accomplished together means even more."

The first half saw both teams generate a few offensive runs and create some prime opportunities to find the game's opening goal. However, both goalkeepers came up with big saves to send the title tilt into halftime knotted at 0-0. Jamestown CC's Angel Busch made multiple diving saves, delivering perhaps her best performance of the season when it mattered most.

"Angel came up big when we needed her to, and that's exactly what you need from your goalkeeper in a championship game," Chimera said. "She made some huge saves in moments when every play mattered, and she gave us the opportunity to keep fighting. I'm really proud of the way she stepped up for her teammates today and came through when we needed her most."

Early in the second half, Busch continued to turn away Mohawk Valley CC's attempts before the Hawks finally broke through in the 50th minute, putting Jamestown in a 1-0 deficit.

With the clock winding down to under 16 minutes and the scoreboard still showing 1-0, a pro-Jamestown CC crowd was inching to the edge of its seats. That's when Avery Johnson found possession inside the box, but before the freshman could get off an attempt, she was pulled to the ground, and Jamestown CC was awarded a penalty kick.

Up stepped Kaylyn Carnes to take the penalty kick. The sophomore approached the ball and blasted a shot toward the bottom-right corner. It slipped just past the Hawks' goalkeeper, sending the green-and-gold faithful into a frenzy as the Jayhawks evened the score at 1-1.

With less than 13 minutes remaining and the game still tied, Ally Notarianni drove hard toward the net, making one of the biggest plays of her Jayhawk career. Her attempt was redirected out of play by the Hawks’ goalkeeper, setting up a crucial corner kick for Jamestown CC.

CASSADAGA — A community is in mourning after a teenager died in an early Saturday morning one-vehicle crash.

Chautauqua County sheriff’s deputies report at 12:37 a.m., they responded with New York State Police, Cassadaga and Stockton Fire Departments to the accident on Maple Avenue. As a result, one male juvenile sustained serious injuries and was flown to an area hospital for treatment. A second male juvenile sustained fatal injuries and was pronounced deceased.

Both involved in the accident were Cassadaga Valley Central School students. In a Facebook post, the district called the news “heartbreaking” and noted it had counseling available on Saturday and Sunday.

“Our hearts are with both families as they navigate this unimaginable tragedy,” the post said. “We ask that our community respect the privacy of both families during this incredibly difficult time.

“We know this news will deeply affect our students, our staff, and our entire community. …

“If you need support, connect with those close to you or our team. There are no perfect words for a moment like this. Today, we simply need to take care of one another, give our students grace, and remember that we are one school community, and we will continue to support one another as we navigate this heartbreaking tragedy.”

As of Sunday morning, the names of those involved in the crash were not released.

The accident remains under investigation by the Chautauqua County Sheriff’s Office. Additional information will be released as it becomes available.

local.body:
PITTSBURGH (AP) -- The Pittsburgh Steelers spent all week hearing the chatter coming from Cleveland, then spent all Sunday emphatically and repeatedly putting their longtime rivals in their place.

Maybe better days are coming for Deshaun Watson, Jared Verse and company. They’re just not here yet.

At least not in Pittsburgh, where the Browns remain the Browns.

Jaylen Warren tied a career high with 143 yards rushing and a touchdown on his 28th birthday, and the Steelers (6-2) moved into first place in the AFC North with a dominant 27-6 victory.

The Steelers sacked Watson eight times, and Pittsburgh piled up 200 yards on the ground to beat the Browns (5-3) for the 23rd straight time in the regular season at Acrisure Stadium, tying the NFL record for consecutive home victories over an opponent. Green Bay won 23 in a row against Detroit from 1992 to 2014.

“It kind of sends a message to the rest of the division, like we’re here to play,” Steelers right guard Brock Hoffman said. “We’re here to be physical. We play the game the right way on both sides of the ball up front, and that’s what we want as our identity.”

It’s an identity Cleveland (5-3) is trying to build, too. The Browns believe they’re on their way, and Verse raised eyebrows in the run-up by saying it was time for Cleveland to take the two-hour drive southeast and “make Pittsburgh ours.”

It didn’t quite turn out like that. It rarely does when the Browns play the Steelers on the road.

local.title: One person dead after fire tore through home in Lockport
local.summary: One person is dead after a fire tore through a home on Park Avenue in Lockport Sunday morning. The cause of the fire is under investigation.
local.body: One person is dead after a fire tore through a home on Park Avenue in Lockport Sunday morning.According to the City of Lockport Fire Department, just after 3:30 a.m., crews responded to a home on 516 Park Avenue with flames visible in the kitchen and one person trapped.Heavy fire was found to be coming from the first and second floor windows of the home. The initial fire attack crew made their way into the first floor to search for the trapped person. The search was hindered by hoarding conditions inside the home.The trapped person was found unconscious and was immediately extricated. Advanced life saving procedures were attempted but the victim was pronounced dead at the scene.A second person was able to exit the home but suffered from second-degree and third-degree burns. Paramedics performed advanced airway procedures and they were taken to ECMC.A third person was able to escape unharmed with a dog out of a first floor window. He was evaluated and released on the scene. Crews worked on the scene for approximately two hours before the fire was declared under control. No firefighters were injured.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

entertainment.title: Jack Lowden Is Tight-Lipped on Those Bond Rumors: “I’m Not Going to Add to the Noise”
entertainment.summary: The 'Slow Horses' star, who is next set to play Mr. Darcy in Netflix's 'Pride and Prejudice' adaptation, admitted the speculation is "very flattering."
entertainment.body:
Logo text Jack Lowden isn’t giving anything away on his rumored screen tests for the role of James Bond .

In an interview with British GQ published on Monday, the Scottish star briefly touches on the reports — including those from The Hollywood Reporter — that he is part of a small group of actors eyed for the next incarnation of Ian Fleming’s beloved spy, next to Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor.

Lowden addresses the viral lines from his Slow Horses co-star Gary Oldman, who set the internet alight a little when he told Canada’s The Morning Show in September that the role had been cast and he was hoping it was Lowden. “They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack,” said the English Oscar-winner. ( THR was later informed by a source that the MI6 agent had not yet been chosen at that time.) Related Stories TV Series' Women Participants Revealed for European Female Leadership Program Movies Tallinn Black Nights Fest Turns 30 With New Artistic Director, a Latin American Streak and a Baltic Boom

“It’s all very flattering,” says Lowden, who proceeded to pour “cold water” on the topic, according to British GQ ‘s Kieran Morris. “It’s nice to be mentioned — for any role — and I’m just not really going to add to the noise,” he continues. “It’s very nice, and Gary’s a sweetheart. It’s particularly lovely, coming from someone like him. But I don’t really listen to it.”

Just last week, THR heard word that screen tests for Amazon MGM Studios’ James Bond film, directed by Dune ‘s Denis Villeneuve and written by Peaky Blinders mastermind Steven Knight, would be taking place in London at the end of October. Jack O’Connell ( Sinners ) was rumored to initially be in the mix, but sources told us that wasn’t the case. And despite some reports, Euphoria and Frankenstein star Jacob Elordi would also not be testing.

The GQ piece made the savvy observation that the woman who cast Lowden in his breakout, Emmy-nominated role as Slow Horses ‘s River Cartwright, Nina Gold, is also leading the search for Daniel Craig’s replacement.

And Lowden’s wife, Irish Oscar nominee Saoirse Ronan, has also been tight-lipped on the speculation. “[That’s] its own thing,” Ronan told the Associated Press in October . “We’re kind of getting on with our life, to be honest. We have plenty of other things to be dealing with. So, yeah, it’s not really a subject that’s coming up in our house, to be honest. The dog needs to be walked, the dinner needs to be made — we’re most focused on that.”

entertainment.body:
Australian metalcore band Thornhill will headline and curate Surf’s Up! Festival , a one-day heavy music event at Melbourne ’s Riviera Beach Club on Saturday, Feb. 20, 2027, promoter Destroy All Lines announced Monday (Nov. 2). Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

The bill, selected by the band, features Stand Atlantic , Alpha Wolf , US duo SACE6, Justice for the Damned, Philadelphia’s Varials, Headwreck, Bloom and Blinder. Presale tickets go on sale Thursday (Nov. 5) at 10 a.m. AEDT, with general tickets following Friday (Nov. 6) at 11 a.m. The event is 18+. Related Suki Waterhouse, Australian Crawl Join Sydney Opera House's On The Steps Series Wu-Tang Clan to Headline Detroit Lions Thanksgiving Game Halftime Show Harry Styles Dresses as NYC 'Pizza Rat,' Gets Jalen Brunson Tribute at Final MSG Residency Show

“Personally curated by the four of us, we are stoked to be joined by some of the best names in Australian heavy music,” Thornhill said in a statement. “Expect big riffs, good times and a whole lot of energy.”

It’s the second artist-curated heavy bill at the St Kilda venue, following a Polaris-programmed edition staged there in February as part of the Life’s A Beach series.

Thornhill arrive off the strongest run of their career. Their third album, Bodies, debuted at No. 4 on the ARIA albums chart in 2025 and won the ARIA Award for best hard rock or heavy metal album, plus best independent heavy album or EP at the AIR Awards. It was also nominated for Australian album of the year at the J Awards. The band’s 2022 album Heroine reached No. 3 on the ARIA chart and No. 1 on the Australian albums chart, earning an ARIA nomination, while 2019 debut The Dark Pool hit No. 20 on the Australian albums chart. They have toured with Sleep Token, Bring Me the Horizon, Architects and Avenged Sevenfold, and played Download, Welcome to Rockville, Hellfest and Graspop Metal Meeting.

Stand Atlantic released their fifth album, Godbreath, on Oct. 23 through Virgin Music Group, and it debuted at No. 1 on the ARIA albums chart last week — the Sydney band’s first chart-topper , eclipsing the No. 3 peak of 2024’s Was Here. They have toured with Sum 41, A Day to Remember and ONE OK ROCK, with a 2026 Warped Tour run and a UK support slot with Simple Plan.

Alpha Wolf earned an ARIA nomination for best hard rock or heavy metal album with 2020’s A Quiet Place to Die and a Grammy nomination for best boxed or special limited edition package for 2024’s Half Living Things. SACE6 released debut album Brutalist this year and have toured with Dayseeker, Don Broco and Northlane. Varials released their fourth album, Where the Light Leaves, in 2026 and are currently on a North American run supporting Wage War.

entertainment.title: Series’ Women Participants Revealed for European Female Leadership Program
entertainment.summary: Germany’s Erich Pommer Institut has unveiled the 15 women producers selected for the sixth edition of its program.
entertainment.body:
Series’ Women , the European female leadership program organized by the Erich Pommer Institut (EPI), has unveiled the 15 female producers from 12 countries that it has selected for its sixth edition.

Launched in 2021, the initiative “supports female producers in advancing their careers, strengthening their professional networks and increasing the visibility of female-driven projects across the European screen industry,” EPI says. The program combines expert-led training in visibility, leadership and digital entrepreneurship with individual mentoring and pitching coaching tailored to participants’ career goals. Exclusive networking opportunities at major European industry markets also provide direct access to key industry players and foster lasting connections. The goal is to strengthen female leadership, promote the professional development of women producers and contribute to greater diversity and representation across the European screen industry. Among the major networking opportunities are TV Drama Vision, presented by the Göteborg Film Festival in Sweden, and Series Mania Forum in Lille, France. Through an online diversity training course designed for hiring managers or decision-makers at the producers’ companies, Series’ Women also looks to address topics of gender equality and diversity at an organizational level. Related Stories Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Crashes Into Tokyo Film Festival With Stars Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe in Tow Music Macklemore Wraps Up Free Palestine Tour in London: "It Was More Uncomfortable for Me to Stay Silent"

“Series’ Women offers female producers a valuable space to exchange experiences, build European networks and strengthen their professional profiles,” said Gabriela Seidel-Hollaender, project manager for the international female leadership programs at the Erich Pommer Institute. “We are proud to offer the program for the sixth time, contributing to a stronger and more sustainable European series industry.”

Series’ Women is funded by Creative Europe – MEDIA. The event partner is Series Mania Forum. entertainment.title: Tallinn Black Nights Fest Turns 30 With New Artistic Director, a Latin American Streak and a Baltic Boom
entertainment.summary: In her first year at the programming helm, Triin Tramberg is making few changes and watching closely to see what works: "I made the decision that this year is really observational for me."
entertainment.body:
Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) is kicking off its 30th edition on Friday, the first under the creative leadership of artistic director Triin Tramberg . The lineup promises a mix of new discoveries and gems, envelope-pushing films and the best of the year’s festival circuit.

The film curator, whose profile has grown alongside PÖFF’s over more than 15 years, began her work at the fest as a program assistant before becoming a program coordinator and playing a key role in shaping Tallinn’s international profile. PÖFF founder and longtime fest director Tiina Lokk , who remains CEO, has shifted her focus to overall strategic and developmental direction. Related Stories Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Crashes Into Tokyo Film Festival With Stars Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe in Tow Music Macklemore Wraps Up Free Palestine Tour in London: "It Was More Uncomfortable for Me to Stay Silent"

The 30th anniversary edition of PÖFF, running Nov. 6-22, will screen 230 feature films and 259 shorts from 87 countries. PÖFF, its youth and children’s film festival Just Film and PÖFF Shorts, which is dedicated to short films, together will present 107 world premieres and 47 international premieres.

The programming lineup of the Tallinn fest has increasingly showcased movies from around the globe, with Latin America having a particularly strong presence this year. But the 30th PÖFF will also proudly put a spotlight on Baltic cinema, covering the fest’s home of Estonia, along with Lithuania and Latvia, which has always been “an essential part of PÖFF,” Tramberg says. Since 2008, the festival has presented the Baltic Film Competition, to which it added a Baltic documentary competition last year. “In our 30th-anniversary year, we want to give it an even stronger international platform and draw attention not only to our films, but also to the remarkable talent behind them,” emphasizes Tramberg. “Giving Baltic cinema a central place in this anniversary programme feels especially meaningful. We want international audiences to discover the diversity of filmmaking in our region, and local audiences to see familiar places and experiences through fresh eyes.”

Beyond that, “this year’s program reflects very different lives and experiences, yet tells stories we can connect with,” she says.

In a chat with THR , Tramberg previewed what to expect from Tallinn 2026, how the Baltics are the new Nordics and why she is keeping a close eye on what works and what doesn’t in her first year.

entertainment.title: Ausify Campaign Returns as Australian Music’s Streaming Share Hits New Low
entertainment.summary: Ben Lee, Missy Higgins and Budjerah are among the artists backing the month-long push, which asks fans to make their support for local music public.
entertainment.body:
Ausify, the national campaign to lift Australian music’s visibility at home, launched its second year Monday (Nov. 2) against a worsening backdrop: local music now accounts for just 8.5% of all audio streamed in Australia.

That figure comes from APRA AMCOS’s latest Year in Review , released in October, which recorded a 37.5% decline in local content’s streaming share over five years, down from 13.6% in FY21. The rights body’s CEO, Dean Ormston, has warned the share could fall to about 5% within five years without intervention. On user-generated content platforms, Australian music’s share sits lower still, at 3.6%. Related Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Jessica Lynch

A separate analysis published by the Australia Institute last year, using IFPI data, found Australian artists’ share of the 10,000 most-streamed acts in Australia fell from 12% to 8% between 2021 and 2024, with the number of Australian acts on that list dropping from 932 to 773.

The campaign frames the problem as discovery rather than demand. A nationally representative survey of 1,018 Australians, conducted by Pureprofile for Music Australia in October, found 84% say a defining life moment brings an Australian song to mind, and two-thirds could name the song. But only 27% say they have streamed an Australian artist in the past 12 months. Earlier research in Music Australia’s Listening In series found 71% feel pride hearing local music, 62% feel a connection to it and rate it as good as international music, and 66% want more of it.

“These positive attitudes are not translating into listening, sharing, attendance and advocacy,” the campaign said in its launch material, pointing to availability, discoverability and default listener behaviors “often influenced by streaming algorithms and dwarfed by artists from larger English-speaking markets.”

Where last year’s campaign asked listeners to “Ausify” their algorithms, this year’s pitch is visibility: Ausify is calling for “Public Displays of Ausify,” from social posts and tour merch to singing along in public. The month-long run launched with seven Australian artists performing a karaoke version of “Love Is in the Air,” and the artists backing it include Ben Lee, Fanny Lumsden, Astrid Jorgensen, aleksiah, Ayesha Madon, Becca Hatch, Budjerah, Conor Jacob Smith of Midnight Til Morning, Georgia Maq, ISHAN, Missy Higgins, Nooky, Ruel and Vv Pete.

entertainment.title: Tokyo: ‘Diamond Diplomacy’ Doc Tracks the History of Baseball in Japan and Its Impact on U.S. Relations
entertainment.summary: Film traces stories of players from both countries crossing the Pacific, racial and diplomatic tensions, wartime baseball, through to the phenomenon that is Shohei Ohtani.
entertainment.body:
Examining 150 years of Japan -US relations through the prism of a common passion for baseball , Diamond Diplomacy deftly interweaves the story of Japanese yakyu with issues of history, geopolitics and race.

Directed by Yuriko Gamo Romer, born in Tokyo but raised in the US, the documentary traces baseball’s 1872 introduction to Japan by an American educator and its integration into the school system, through the development of pro teams and the eventual flow of Japanese players to the major leagues. Along the way were tours to Japan by Babe Ruth – credited, perhaps hyperbolically, for delaying war between the US and Japan – and the importance of baseball for Japanese-Americans, through to the superstar status of Shohei Ohtani . Related Stories Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Crashes Into Tokyo Film Festival With Stars Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe in Tow Music Macklemore Wraps Up Free Palestine Tour in London: "It Was More Uncomfortable for Me to Stay Silent"

“People from MLB told me that I had great timing and was making the film at just the right moment with Ohtani’s success,” said Romer at a screening before the film’s official Japan premiere at Tokyo International Film Festival. “But it was just coincidence. I started researching this film 12 years ago and it took me years of making money and raising money to fund it.”

Having landed a $600,000 National Endowment for the Humanities grant, more than half of the funding was cancelled in April 2025 as swingeing DOGE cuts suddenly took effect. Former American diplomat Glen S. Fukushima stepped in with $300,000 that allowed the film to be finished.

Author Robert Whiting, whose books helped introduce the peculiarities of baseball in Japan to the wider world, is one of the documentary’s talking heads.

“Japanese baseball is older than judo,” notes Whiting in the film, going on to suggest that perfectionist methods and obsessive mindsets adapted from martial arts helped mold baseball in Japan.

Footage of Babe Ruth’s 1934 tour leading an all-star American League team shows the wild enthusiasm of huge crowds that turned out to see the visitors as they played against and alongside Japanese players even amidst rising political tensions that would soon culminate in war. Ruth is reported to have thrown all his Japan souvenirs out of his apartment window when he heard the news of the attack on Pearl Harbor.

Romer’s previous documentary Baseball Behind Barbed Wire told how Japanese-Americans interned during World War Two played games inside the camps, which she covers in the new film, along with how baseball was a bulwark against postwar prejudice.

entertainment.title: Marty Erlichman, Barbra Streisand’s Longtime Manager, Dies at 97
entertainment.summary: An entertainment manager for decades, Erlichman also worked with The Clancy Brothers and Tommy Makem.
entertainment.body:
Martin Lee “Marty” Erlichman, Barbra Streisand ‘s manager for more than six decades, died on Oct. 31. He was 97.

Erlichman’s death was due to “age-related causes,” a press release issued on Sunday (Nov. 1) states.

As an entertainment manager, Erlichman is credited with discovering Streisand and helping to shape and guide her career since the early 1960s.

Erlichman was born in Brooklyn, New York, on Sept. 13, 1929, and is an alumni of Drake University in Des Moines, Iowa. He’s the recipient of both an Emmy Award and a Peabody Award for his work as executive producer of the 1994 HBO television special Barbra: The Concert .

He first encountered Streisand when she was 19 years old and singing as the opening act for comedian Phil Leeds at Bon Soir nightclub in Greenwich Village. Streisand has recalled that her soon-to-be new manager told her he got chills the moment he heard her vocals; she felt comfortable with him immediately, feeling he “validated all my dreams” while being “like a guy from my old neighborhood. Turns out he grew up near me in Brooklyn. We spoke the same language.”

He helped her secure her first recording contract, with Columbia Records. Streisand is thankful he negotiated giving her creative control on her repertoire and album covers, “an unprecedented contract for a first-timer.”

“Although Marty lived a long and full life, nothing can prepare you for the reality of losing someone so dear,” Streisand said in a statement following Erlichman’s passing. “I truly thought he would live forever. In my eyes, he was simply indestructible — always by my side, through everything. And we never even had a contract. Marty can never be replaced, and I will be forever grateful for his friendship, loyalty, and unwavering support.”

Streisand also said, “A few weeks ago, he was trying to convince me to go on tour, and told me he’d be there every step of the way. I know it’s extremely rare for show business relationships to endure for as long as mine did with Marty. He trusted me, and I trusted him. This is a challenging business, but I always felt protected with Marty by my side.”

entertainment.title: Marty Erlichman, Barbra Streisand’s Longtime Manager, Dies at 97
entertainment.summary: He discovered the singer at 19 years old and managed her career for more than six decades.
entertainment.body:
Marty Erlichman, the talent manager who discovered Barbra Streisand at age 19 and guided her career for more than six decades, has died. He was 97.

Erlichman died Saturday of “age-related causes,” according to a statement from his reps.

“To the world, he was a giant of Hollywood; to us, he was a deeply devoted and loving father, husband, grandfather and rock,” Erlichman’s family said in a statement. “We feel his loss deeply but are endlessly proud of the life he lived and the indelible mark he left on the world.” Related Stories Music Timbaland Files $15 Million Fraud Lawsuit Against Former Managers TV Bobby Wright, 'McHale's Navy' Actor, Singer and Son of Kitty Wells, Dies at 84

Said Streisand: “Although Marty lived a long and full life, nothing can prepare you for the reality of losing someone so dear. I truly thought he would live forever. In my eyes, he was simply indestructible — always by my side, through everything. And we never even had a contract. Marty can never be replaced, and I will be forever grateful for his friendship, loyalty and unwavering support.”

Erlichman discovered Streisand and help guide her from an aspiring New York nightclub singer into a global star, serving as her manager for more than 60 years. He oversaw the business side of her career, negotiating her recording, theater, film, television, licensing and concert agreements.

Erlichman conceived and executive produced Streisand’s concert appearances and tours including her 2000 Millennium Concert and her 2006–07 world tour. He also served as executive producer of her 1994 HBO television special, Barbra: The Concert, which earned him an Emmy Award and a Peabody Award.

Born September 13, 1929, in Brooklyn, New York, Erlichman graduated from Drake University in Des Moines, Iowa. Early in his career, in 1960, he began managing the pioneering Irish folk group The Clancy Brothers and Tommy Makem, whose music went on to influence Bob Dylan. In 1961, Erlichman secured the group a spot on The Ed Sullivan Show. They were supposed to perform only two songs but were given extra time when fellow guest Pearl Bailey failed to appear. The group was allowed to perform for 20 minutes, helped lead to a recording contract with Columbia Records.

That May, Mr. Erlichman went to the Bon Soir nightclub in Greenwich Village to support his friend, comedian Phil Leeds. The opening act was Streisand, who was then 19 years old. Streisand later recalled his enthusiasm for her talent, but she told him she was an actress, and performing as a singer only because she wasn’t landing any acting jobs.

entertainment.title: Martha Stewart Responds to Backlash Over Halloween Costume Depicting Homeless Person: “Never My Intention”
entertainment.summary: In the since-deleted photo, the lifestyle guru appears to be wearing ripped clothing and holding a clipboard with the message, "I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!"
entertainment.body:
Martha Stewart is addressing the backlash over a since-deleted photo of her Halloween costume, where she appears to be depicting a homeless person.

In the photo posted on Instagram before being quickly deleted, TMZ reported that the lifestyle guru and media mogul was seen in ripped clothing with dirt on her face. She was also holding a clipboard with a message that read “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!”

In a statement to People , Stewart said she’s “distressed” that her Halloween costume offended people, as she intended to raise awareness about homelessness. Related Stories Music Harry Styles Goes Full Pizza Rat for Halloween at Final MSG Show, Jalen Brunson Makes Surprise Visit Movies 'You Can See Everything,' 'Clayface' Fighting for No. 1 in Quiet Halloween Weekend

“I’ve spent decades teaching others how to celebrate Halloween — sharing fun, festive recipes, providing unique craft ideas and giving tips on entertaining and hosting to make the most of one of my favorite holidays of the year,” she said. “I am distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention. “Homelessness continues to remain one of America’s greatest challenges and ongoing crises, something that I care deeply about and I have spent a significant amount of time and effort supporting charities that combat this ongoing social epidemic,” Stewart continued. “I am committed to continuing to make a difference.”

The Hollywood Reporter has also reached out to Stewart’s rep for comment.

TMZ reported that the photo was included in an Instagram carousel promoting candles she sells on QVC. “My QVC candles are perfect for Halloween!!!!!” the post’s caption read.

After screenshots of the photo started circulating on social media, people didn’t hold back on their criticism. “Martha Stewart absolutely tone deaf and totally out of touch. Absolutely shameful,” one person wrote on X. Another person said, “Mocking homelessness is not okay or funny.”

entertainment.title: Wu-Tang Clan to Headline Detroit Lions Thanksgiving Game Halftime Show
entertainment.summary: They'll take the halftime performance slot at the Nov. 26 Lions-Bears game, while Antonio Cipriano will perform the national anthem.
entertainment.body:
Wu-Tang Clan is set to headline the Detroit Lions’ halftime show on Thanksgiving, when the team takes on the Chicago Bears at Ford Field.

Actor and recording artist Antonio Cipriano ( Off Campus , Broadway’s Jagged Little Pill ), a native of Michigan, is singing the national anthem at Ford Field ahead of the Detroit Lions Thanksgiving Day Classic presented by Ford, which is scheduled to air on CBS at 1 p.m. ET. on Nov. 26.

For the second year, Eminem and Paul Rosenberg, his manager and president of Shady Records, chose the Lions’ halftime show talent as executive producers of the show.

“We often like to do things that are both exciting and unexpected,” said Rosenberg in a press release issued on Sunday (Nov. 1). “A Wu-Tang Clan Thanksgiving performance in Detroit certainly fits that description! Both Eminem and myself have been Wu fans since the early ’90s along with a whole generation of Detroit football fans, and we are honored to bring them to this year’s stage.”

Wu-Tang — RZA, GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, U-God, Masta Killa, Inspectah Deck, Cappadonna and the late Ol’ Dirty Bastard (ODB) — are members of the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, set to be inducted at the Nov. 14 ceremony in Los Angeles. The group just wrapped its Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber Tour.

“Our Thanksgiving Day Classic is one of the greatest traditions in sports, and Wu-Tang Clan is one of the greatest performers in music,” said Detroit Lions president and CEO Rich Haddad on Sunday. “We are thrilled to have Wu-Tang headlining our Thanksgiving halftime show and grateful to Marshall and Paul for their partnership.”

Last year, Jack White headlined the team’s Thanksgiving halftime show, sharing the stage with special guest Eminem.
